messages_body:
Hi Mina,

Thanks for the intro — I work on procurement at NovaScale. We're finalizing an Azure private offer (reserved nodes + on-demand burst) and I want to understand a couple of specifics before we send a PO: 

1) Prepay bucketization: we plan to prepay a fixed 12-month spend bucket that covers core reserved capacity, with an ability to draw down on that bucket for bursts. Is there an established mapping you use on the Redwood side between prepay buckets and marketplace SKUs so usage is charged against the prepay first? We have divergent SKU families for reserved vs burst and want predictable invoice routing.

2) Reseller uplift / channel split: our reseller partner will invoice us and expects a fixed % uplift on the list price as part of their services. We need clarity on whether Redwood can surface a separate invoice line or a pass-through credit so the reseller uplift doesn't get commingled with the Redwood list price on the marketplace settlement.

Attached is a 6-month usage forecast (very rough). Can you confirm what information Redwood needs for: SKU mapping, prepay aliasing, and evidence for reseller pass-through routing?

Goal: get enough detail to draft a PO that avoids manual month-end reconciliations.

Thanks,
James Neal
Procurement Manager, NovaScale
attach: Novascale-usage-forecast.xlsx

Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: James Neal <james.neal@novascale.com>, NovaScale Procurement <procurement@novascale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: structuring prepay buckets + reseller uplift for Azure private offer

Thanks James — great, and appreciate the forecast. Quick answers and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Prepay bucketization: yes, we can alias a prepay bucket to a set of SKUs. On the Azure marketplace this is normally done by mapping the prepaid commitment to the primary reserved SKU family; burst usage hits the compatible on-demand SKU and is invoiced against consumption. We'll create a mapping table in the private offer so that prepay draws down first.
- Reseller uplift: we can't change the marketplace settlement flow, but we can: 1) add a discrete "reseller_pass_through" line in our billing metadata and 2) provide a weekly settlement report that your reseller can use to reconcile uplift invoicing. If you need the reseller uplift to be excluded from Redwood's listed price for marketplace settlement, that requires the reseller to invoice separately — we can provide per-line evidence to support that.

What we need from you to lock this down:
- Confirm which reserved SKU families should be included in the prepay alias. (column A in your forecast would be ideal)
- Confirm the uplift % your reseller is expecting and whether they want it on reserved capacity, burst, or both.
- If you need an explicit pass-through line on our metadata, confirm the reseller's legal entity name and billing tax ID.

Action items:
- I'll draft a private-offer configuration and attach a proposed PDF (for internal review) that shows mapping and the billing metadata.
- Ben (cc) will verify tax handling and pass-through feasibility with finance.

I'll follow up with a proposal by EOD tomorrow. If you prefer a quick call to walk through the mapping table, I'm available 11:30–12:30 PT.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (555) 614-0210

Mina — quick fiscal note from finance: we can expose a reseller_pass_through metadata key in billing exports and generate a weekly CSV for NovaScale's reseller reconciliation. Two caveats:

1) Market settlement: Azure marketplace gross settlement will still show the Redwood list price and Redwood as the transacting provider. Any reseller uplift that NovaScale wants billed separately must come from the reseller's own invoice. Our docs + the weekly CSV should be sufficient evidence for their accounting, but we can't alter marketplace gross receipts.

2) Tax & VAT handling: if the reseller pass-through is required to be outside Redwood's tax boundary, we'll need the reseller tax ID and local VAT registration details before we finalize the private offer metadata. Without that, our default tax flow applies.

Connor — can you pull the prepay alias template I used with another customer (tabbed SKU mapping + fallback rules) and drop it into the proposed-private-offer-draft.pdf Mina is preparing? James — once that's in the draft, we can include a redlined clause that states "reseller uplift to be invoiced separately by reseller; Redwood will provide per-line usage evidence."

I flagged this with collections and they said timelines look good as long as we get reseller tax info within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Deal Ops, Redwood Inference
